newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index slips as VUB Bank share falls.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index slips as VUB Bank share falls.

text.p: Slovak top stocks remained mired in sluggish trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange on Friday, and the official 16-share SAX index slipped 1.22 points to close the week at 169.34.
The biggest loser among the main market shares in Friday's continuous trading session was VUB Bank VSEO.BV which fell 172 crowns to 1,062, but only on a trade of two shares.

"There were several declines today, for example average price of builder Vahostav fell by 16.9 percent, but traded volumes do not indicate any fundamental reasons for such moves," said Creditanstalt's chief trader Peter Krutil.
Steel maker VSZ, which has been considered the BSE's most liquid share over the past few months, eased by five crowns to 645, on trade of 51 shares.
The most-heavily weighted issue, oil refiner Slovnaft, closed up 25 at 875, with 150 shares changing hands.
"In general, price movements often fail to indicate shares' fundamentals due to lucklastre trading activity and low volumes," Krutil said.

Overall volume rose to 2,053,249 shares from 164,969 stocks traded on Thursday, but mainly boosted by block transfers of holdings inside the portfolio of the larges investment fund VUB Kupon, dealers said.
Hence, turnover jumped to 1.597 billion crowns from 65.841 million on Thursday.
